statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1, assume in addition that PHy = 0 and r = ∥x∥ > 0, and put ∆ = R2 − r2. Fix a head norming test p = PHp with ρ(p) = 1 and x(p) = r. For every finite ancestral K ⊃ H and each sign τ ∈ {−1, 1}, choose any finite law of represented vectors A = ∑︂ i aidSi , ∑︂ i a2 i ≤ R2 , Eτ A = PK(x + τy), where each represented family consists of disjoint segments. Put bi = rp(Si), A◦ = ∑︂ i bidSi , V = ∑︂ i (ai − bi)2 , L = r2 − ∑︂ i b2 i . 29 These laws exist by the finite atomic-ball formula. For every such choice, the replacement satisfies Eτ (V + L) ≤ ∆, Eτ ∥QH(A − A◦ )∥ ≤ √ ∆. (13.1) At each gate g, let b(g) be the replaced crossing coefficient, or zero when there is no crossing segment. The mixed absolute crossing vector m(g) = (︁ E1|b(g)|+E−1|b(g)| )︁ /2 satisfies ∥m∥2 ≤ √ 2∆. Consequently a separate endpoint argument, followed by ancestral exhaustion, yields ∥y∥ ≤ (1 + 2 √ 2) √ ∆. (13.2) If the same two nonnegative errors are bounded separately, without retaining their sum, the corresponding calculation gives ∥y∥ ≤ (1 + 2 √ 3) √ ∆. (13.3)
